name: CF Industries Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: CF Industries is a global producer and distributor of hydrogen and nitrogen products: anhydrous ammonia, granular urea, UAN, ammonium nitrate and diesel exhaust fluid. Its customers include agricultural cooperatives, distributors and industrial users, and its manufacturing complexes are in North America and the UK. Christopher Bohn, a 17-year CF veteran and former CFO, became CEO in January 2026, succeeding Tony Will. The company is building Blue Point One, a low-carbon ammonia joint venture with JERA and Mitsui (CF owns 40%), at Modeste, Louisiana, with production expected in 2029. Q2 2026 net sales were $2.22B, up 17.6% YoY, on tight global nitrogen markets.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): CF formed the Blue Point One JV with JERA (35%) and Mitsui (25%) in April 2025 and broke ground in August 2026 on what partners call the world's largest low-carbon ammonia plant (about 1.4M tons a year, about $3.7B to $4B, Topsoe autothermal reforming) [4]. That opens a new clean-energy revenue stream beyond fertilizer, alongside a low-carbon UAN collaboration with PepsiCo [3]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI products shipping to customers and no quantified AI-driven savings were found. Market Share (2/2): CF is a scale leader in North American nitrogen. TTM revenue of $7.74B and a 27% net margin reflect a structurally advantaged low-cost gas position that defines the regional market [1][2]. Pipeline (2/2): Blue Point One has state and federal permits (July 2026), named offtakers (JERA about 490K tons a year for its Hekinan power station) and a 2029 start date. A roughly $100M CO2 dehydration and compression project is also under way at Yazoo City [4]. R&D Intensity (0/1): FMP reports R&D-to-revenue of 0% [2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): CF frames its purpose around providing clean energy to feed and fuel the world sustainably, which connects nitrogen to food security and decarbonization, echoed in its self-description as a producer of 'hydrogen and nitrogen products' for energy, fertilizer and emissions reduction [6]. The statement is clear but not distinctive among fertilizer and energy peers. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive foundation or quantified community investment program was found in the research. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found. The orderly internal CEO succession (Bohn joined in 2009 and was promoted from CFO) points to stability but does not count as retention data [5]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying by the new CEO or other executives was found.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on the Growth sleeve formula, because the roughly 1.8% yield ($2.10 annualized on $118.09) is below the 2% Dividend threshold [6]. D/E of 62.9% ($3.61B of total debt against $5.75B of stockholders' equity) scores 1.0 [2]. TTM ROE of 40.4% scores 1.0 at 2x weight. Q2 2026 revenue growth of 17.6% YoY ($2.222B vs $1.890B) scores 1.0, and the 5-year revenue CAGR of 11.4% (FY2020 $4.12B to FY2025 $7.08B) scores 1.0 at 2x weight [1][2]. A forward P/E of 10.1 (FY2027 consensus EPS $11.66) and a TTM profit margin of 27.1% ($2.10B on $7.74B) each score 1.0 [2][7]. Forward PEG is negative (-0.45) because consensus EPS falls 23% from $15.07 in FY2026 to $11.66 in FY2027, so that 2x-weight metric scores 0 [7]. Weighted sum is 8.0 of 10, for a score of 8. Liquidity is about $292M a day.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): CF's business is converting natural gas into ammonia and upgraded nitrogen products in capital-intensive chemical complexes, then moving them by pipeline, barge and rail. AI cannot substitute for that physical chemistry, and global crop production needs nitrogen regardless of technology cycles [1]. No analyst commentary flagging AI displacement risk was found. The main indirect effect is that AI data-center power demand could tighten U.S. natural gas markets and raise feedstock costs, which affects margin rather than the business model. AI Opportunity (0/1): CF reports no AI-related revenue [2].

infinite_game.summary: Sinek would see a disciplined, well-run commodity producer making some real long-horizon moves, chiefly the Blue Point One low-carbon ammonia JV with a 2029 start and the Yazoo City carbon capture investment. Its identity, though, is still built on cost position and capital returns more than on a Just Cause. Share count has fallen from 215M in 2020 to about 154M as buybacks absorb cash. Political accusations of fertilizer price gouging in 2026 add a finite-game image problem.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Feeding and fueling the world with clean nitrogen and hydrogen is a meaningful idea, and the low-carbon ammonia strategy partly reflects it [1][4]. Leadership still frames value creation mainly through cost advantage and shareholder returns, and in March 2026 Sen. Hawley accused CF of price gouging farmers, which suggests the cause is not understood as service by key stakeholders [3].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership continuity is strong. Tony Will led from 2014 to January 2026 and handed over to Chris Bohn, who joined in 2009 and rose through corporate planning, clean energy leadership and CFO [5]. The predecessor was credited with a 'high-performance culture.' No employee engagement or turnover data was found to support a high-trust rating.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Competitive framing centers on structural cost advantages over European and Asian producers and on capturing pricing in a tight market [3]. No management commentary acknowledging rivals' strengths as a spur to improvement was found.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): CF is extending from agricultural nitrogen into low-carbon ammonia as an energy carrier. JERA will take about 490K tons a year from Blue Point One for co-firing at its Hekinan power station [4]. The underlying process (ammonia from natural gas, now with carbon capture) is unchanged, so this is an adjacent-market evolution rather than reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Committing CF's 40% share of a $3.7B to $4B plant that will not produce until 2029, and choosing blue over green ammonia on economic grounds, is a real long-cycle bet [3][4]. Large ongoing buybacks (weighted shares down from 168.6M in Q1 2025 to 153.6M in Q2 2026) show the bet is funded from surplus rather than through near-term sacrifice [2].

investment_thesis: CF is earning near peak-cycle economics. Q2 2026 net sales rose 17.6% to $2.22B and diluted EPS doubled to $4.73 (from $2.37), as Iran-related supply disruptions tightened an already tight global nitrogen market [1][3]. TTM net income of $2.10B on $7.74B of revenue (27% margin), 40% ROE and only $1.13B of net debt support aggressive capital return; weighted shares fell from 168.6M to 153.6M in five quarters [2]. At 8.7x trailing and 10.1x forward earnings, roughly 4.6x EV/EBITDA, and a 10.7% FCF yield, the stock prices in substantial normalization [2][7]. Blue Point One, with permits secured, construction started in August 2026 and offtake contracted with JERA, gives CF a first-mover position in low-carbon ammonia from 2029 [4].
thesis_continued: The bear case is cyclicality. Consensus expects EPS to fall from $15.07 in FY2026 to $11.66 in FY2027 and about $8.80 by 2030, which means today's earnings are a peak rather than a new baseline [7]. Revenue history shows how quickly that can unwind: $6.54B (2021), $11.19B (2022), $5.94B (2024) [2]. Q2 2026 sales volumes fell 15% and revenue missed the roughly $2.45B consensus, so pricing alone is carrying growth [3]. Political risk is rising, with Sen. Hawley's March 2026 price-gouging accusations and reports of a DOJ fertilizer-pricing probe [3]. Blue Point One also concentrates execution risk in a $3.7B to $4B project whose economics depend on unproven low-carbon ammonia demand and carbon-credit policy [4].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 earnings in early November 2026, where consensus of about $2.99 EPS compares with $2.19 a year ago, testing whether Iran-related nitrogen tightness is still lifting realized prices [3]
Blue Point One construction progress (groundbreaking August 2026, 1.4M tons a year, start-up 2029) with contracted JERA offtake of about 490K tons a year for power-sector ammonia co-firing [4]
Continued share count reduction (weighted shares down from 215M in FY2020 to 153.6M in Q2 2026) funded by about $1.9B of TTM free cash flow to equity [2]
key_risks: Nitrogen price normalization: consensus EPS falls 23% from FY2026 to FY2027 and about 42% by 2030, and history shows revenue can halve within two years ($11.19B in 2022 to $5.94B in 2024) [2][7]
Political and antitrust exposure from Sen. Hawley's March 2026 fertilizer price-gouging accusations and reported DOJ scrutiny of U.S. fertilizer pricing [3]

Blue Point One execution and demand risk on a $3.7B to $4B JV whose returns depend on low-carbon ammonia premiums, 45Q carbon-capture credits and Japanese co-firing demand that are not yet proven at scale [4]
